newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam, China agree to speed up border talks.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, China agree to speed up border talks.

text.p: Vietnam and China have agreed to accelerate the pace of talks aimed at settling disputes over their common land and maritime borders, Vietnam's official media said on Monday.

The reports said Deputy Foreign Minister Vu Khoan met his Chinese counterpart, Tang Jiaxuan, on the sidelines of talks on territorial issues between China and members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

"It was agreed to quicken the tempo of negotiations for the settlement of issues relating to the common land border as well as delineation of the sea boundary in the Bac Bo (Tonkin) Gulf, while exchanging views about other maritime issues," the daily Vietnam News said.
Tension between Hanoi and Beijing over competing sovereignty claims boiled over last month after a Chinese oil rig started drilling in a South China Sea area Vietnam claims as its own.
The rig was withdrawn less than a month later, but the two sides failed to resolve their differences on the issue at an emergency meeting in Beijing two weeks ago.
The potential wealth in oil and natural gas of the offshore areas claimed by Vietnam and China has been a constant threat to recent efforts by both countries to boost ties.
Both claim parts of the Tonkin Gulf and the Paracel and Spratly islands chains, whose ownership is also contested by severak other regional claimants.
Fishing rights in the waters between the two countries are also a long-time dispute.
An official in the coastal city of Danang in central Vietnam said on Monday that authorities intercepted five Chinese fishing boats last week and detained 68 fishermen.

Officials said a similar incident, involving four Chinese fishing vessels and one from Hong Kong, had occured ja month earlier. However, the 62 fishermen arrested in March were fined $3,000 per boat and then released.

Last week's talks between China and the ASEAN nations -- Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- was the third such meeting and the first since ASEAN granted China full membership last July.

On Friday, Beijing reiterated its position on the border and territory disputes with the ASEAN nations, and both sides agreed to address such disputes through dialogue and to prevent differences from hampering relations.

Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, all claimants to the Spratly islands, have been disturbed in the past by what they see as China's increasingly blatant attempts to claim the potentially oil-rich archipelago of coral reefs and atolls.
